headline: ALKANE HITS 1,360 g/t GOLD AT CUFFLEY — UNMINED HIGH-GRADE POD DISCOVERED AND INTEGRATED INTO COSTERFIELD MINE PLAN
snippet: Alkane Resources (ASX: ALK) revealed a new high-grade gold-antimony domain in an unmined section of the Cuffley Lode at its operating Costerfield mine in Victoria, Australia — a zone previously classified as low-grade due to misinterpretation of a crosscutting fault. Hole AD270 returned 580.9 g/t gold and 24% antimony over 0.61 metres, including a peak intercept of 1,360 g/t gold and 19.7% antimony over 0.25 metres, with other holes returning 168.9 g/t gold over 0.9 metres and 60.1 g/t gold over 1.26 metres. The Cuffley pod has already been integrated into the Costerfield mine schedule — meaning this is immediate mine-life value, not a speculative target — and the Sub KC domain at depth continues to deliver additional high-grade infill results, extending both the vertical and lateral envelope of one of Australia's highest-grade operating gold-antimony producers.

headline: CRITICAL ELEMENTS EXPANDS ROSE WEST LITHIUM ZONE 3X TO 1,250m x 800m — 2.70% Li2O OVER 10.5m IN 10,000-METRE QUÉBEC DRILL PROGRAM
snippet: Critical Elements Lithium Corporation (TSX-V: CRE) released Phase 2 assay results from its 10,000-metre summer drill program at the Rose West lithium discovery in Eeyou Istchee, Québec, with hole RW-26-35A returning up to 2.70% Li2O over 10.50 metres and additional holes reporting 1.0–1.9% Li2O over 14–27 metre widths across pegmatites 2, 3, and 5. The mineralized footprint has expanded from 450 x 370 metres to 1,250 x 800 metres — a tripling of the interpreted zone area — with consistent thicknesses of 10 to 40 metres throughout. The program targets a potential 1,250 x 2,000 metre final footprint, positioning Rose West as one of Canada's more systematically advanced new lithium discoveries at a time when lithium carbonate has recovered to CNY 160,500/t, up 94.56% year over year, and with both Mineral Resources' Bald Hill restart and Core Lithium's Finniss restart signalling that the spodumene market has shifted from oversupply to structural restocking demand.

headline: HOT CHILI CONFIRMS HIGH-GRADE CORE REMAINS OPEN AT LA VERDE — 472m AT 0.41% CuEq INCLUDING 105.8m AT 0.70% FROM 397m IN ATACAMA PORPHYRY
snippet: Hot Chili Limited (ASX: HCH / TSX-V: HCH) released step-out drill results from the La Verde copper-gold porphyry discovery in Chile's coastal Atacama region, with hole DKD060 intersecting 472 metres grading 0.41% copper-equivalent from 49 metres depth, including a high-grade core of 105.8 metres at 0.70% CuEq from 397 metres — confirming that the deposit's highest-grade mineralisation remains open at depth and to extensions. The 472-metre continuous intercept at La Verde represents the kind of porphyry footprint scale that warrants district-level resource evaluation, and at copper above $6.58 per pound, the economics of advancing a 0.40%+ CuEq open-pittable system in a Tier 1 Chilean mining jurisdiction are materially different from where they were 18 months ago. For investors tracking copper supply-side additions against the Kamoa-Kakula flood shortfall and the Codelco multi-year underperformance, La Verde sits at the intersection of exploration-stage upside and near-term development catalysts.

headline: GDXJ SURGES 22% IN FIVE SESSIONS TO $116.78 — JUNIOR MINERS OUTRUN SENIOR PRODUCERS AS GDX RECORDS LARGEST SINGLE-DAY RETAIL INFLOW IN OVER A YEAR
snippet: The VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ) climbed 22.42% over the past five trading sessions to $116.78 per unit, outpacing the senior-focused GDX's 21.09% advance to $89.73 — a leverage ratio consistent with the pattern of junior and mid-tier producers amplifying gold's moves through margin expansion when bullion crosses a significant price threshold. GDX recorded $25 million in single-day retail inflows on Friday August 21, the largest intake in at least a year, and has accumulated $419 million in August retail flows that are on pace for the ETF's strongest monthly intake since February 2026. The retail-inflow acceleration comes precisely when the equity-to-bullion ratio still shows gold producers trading well below their 2011 cycle highs relative to the metal price — a valuation asymmetry that active retail traders appear to be acting on, with the junior sub-sector providing the highest operational leverage as gold mines costs into Q3 at $4,650+ spot.

headline: GOLDSILVER.COM: WARSH'S FIRST JACKSON HOLE ADDRESS IS THE HIGHEST-UNCERTAINTY FED SPEECH IN A DECADE — TWO SCENARIOS AND WHAT BOTH MEAN FOR JUNIOR MINERS
snippet: GoldSilver.com argues that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's August 28 address at Jackson Hole carries more genuine uncertainty than any Fed speech since 2022, because Warsh — who took office May 22, 2026 — has no established policy record for markets to anchor on and has sent mixed signals on rate direction since his inauguration. The piece maps two scenarios: a hawkish tilt (no rate cuts signalled through 2027) that would trigger a $150-200 pullback in gold to the $4,450-$4,500 structural support zone before the bull trend resumes; and a neutral or dovish signal that validates the debasement trade and likely pushes gold toward the May $4,832 record by year-end. The analysis argues that retail investors in TSX-V and ASX junior miners should use any Jackson Hole-driven correction as a defined re-entry point at structural support — not an exit signal — because the underlying fiscal drivers of the bull market (U.S. debt load, Treasury buyback expansion, central bank accumulation) exist entirely independent of near-term rate policy.

headline: DOE'S $500M GRANTS SPARK DOMESTIC RARE EARTH RALLY: USAR +8%, CRML +10%, MP MATERIALS +5% — SHAREHOLDER VOTE THURSDAY AUG 28 ADDS CATALYST LAYER
snippet: Critical minerals equities surged Friday August 21 following the U.S. Department of Energy's announcement of $500 million in grants for seven domestic battery-materials and critical-minerals processing companies — USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) gained 8-13%, Critical Metals (NASDAQ: CRML) climbed 10%, and MP Materials (NYSE: MP) advanced 5% as the DOE allocation signalled sustained federal commitment to reducing Chinese supply-chain dependence. Sector catalysts in 2026 have included a $12 billion Trump strategic stockpile plan in February, a China rare earth export ban in June, and a Section 232 critical minerals action in January, with each policy announcement driving measurable institutional and retail inflows into the space. An upcoming USAR shareholder vote on August 28 — combined with the pre-Jackson Hole macro backdrop positioning hard assets favourably — keeps the rare earth equities complex as one of the highest-beta expressions of the U.S. resource security trade entering the final week of August.

headline: GOLD & SILVER STAGING THEIR MOST POWERFUL SIMULTANEOUS BREAKOUT SINCE 2020 — WHAT THE TECHNICAL STRUCTURE SAYS ABOUT WHAT COMES NEXT
snippet: A GoldSeek technical analysis argues that gold and silver are currently staging their most technically significant simultaneous breakout since the 2020 bull run, with both metals holding critical levels that — if sustained over the next ten trading sessions above $4,500 spot gold and $67 spot silver — would confirm new 2026 cycle highs and likely trigger the next institutional repricing of mining equities. The analysis highlights that unlike previous 2026 rallies where gold led and silver lagged, the current advance features silver outperforming at nearly 20% month-over-month versus gold's 15%, a ratio consistent with late-stage bull phases where retail demand and industrial absorption begin compounding each other. For junior mining investors, the piece identifies the structural implication: a confirmed dual breakout in gold and silver simultaneously creates a favourable backdrop for both gold-dominant and silver-dominant project developers on TSX-V and ASX, removing the typical sector rotation headwind where money moves between the two metals rather than flowing into both.

headline: KITCO AM REPORT: GOLD NEARS $4,660 AS PCE WEDNESDAY AND WARSH FRIDAY FRAME WEEK'S DEFINING FED TRADE — CASE FOR BUYING ANY DIP
snippet: Kitco's Monday August 24 morning report placed spot gold at $4,677.14 — its highest level since May 14 — and mapped the two decisive macro events of the week: Core PCE inflation data arriving Wednesday morning (forecast to accelerate to 0.3%) and Fed Chair Warsh's inaugural Jackson Hole address Friday at approximately 10 a.m. ET. Kitco analysts note the PCE-Warsh combination creates a stagflation setup that is broadly gold-positive regardless of outcome: accelerating inflation reinforces the real asset demand thesis while a growth slowdown (Q2 GDP revised lower) supports flight-to-quality positioning. The report also noted spot gold's 1.5% advance Monday — reaching its highest level since May — as the U.S. Dollar Index continued its pre-Jackson Hole slide, with the Treasury buyback program's yield-compression effect creating a mechanical support floor for gold independent of the Fed speech outcome.
